# Charter — S19 Eval Builder (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

- **Project:** S19 'Eval builder', track v1, ADM phase G, delivery plateau, tranche 8, plan `docs/plans/slices/S19-eval-builder.md`.
- **Sponsor:** the programme's sponsoring group, through the tranche-8 PI plan and the standing delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`.
- **Authority:** SPEC V2 §3 D25 with §5.2, §5.7, §6 and the §8 S19 definition. S19 ports no old surface, so its parity id is `PENDING-S0` and nothing in the plan is a re-implementation of an existing product.
- **Objective:** the `claude-api` `build-eval` and `eval-audit` methods become an ordinary product surface. A person defines one flow, builds an input set, signs off the inputs, chooses metrics and a grader, signs off the grading, runs a pilot and then a baseline, and reads a report — all against rows, not against a `.claude/hillclimb/<flow>/` directory of `results.jsonl`, `traces/` and `report.html`.
- **Scope:** the ten tables of `02-DATA-ARCHITECTURE §2.19`; the `approval.eval_id` column and `uq_appr_eval_pending`; thirty-three actions, three scopes and seven events; four jobs; three built-in versioned prompts; screens 15–20 declared for S12; parts A (define, inputs, sign-off), B (run, grade, capture) and C (report, audit, interop).
- **Acceptance:** the twelve-step gate of the plan's §7, carried by `acceptance/programme/S19.toml`, whose P0 checks are the project row, the approved baseline, the charter asset, the delivery contract, the Phase-G review, the waivers, the PI cadence, plan and objectives, the WSJF inputs, the demo credits, the product findings, the artefact standard and the rework resolution.
- **Status:** the project stays active. This charter, the lifecycle set that follows and the two declared outputs are authored retrospectively for the tranche-8 rework; they record what the pinned snapshot holds and do not claim the product's twelve-step gate has been re-run for the pack.

soaw.title: Statement of Architecture Work — S19 Eval Builder (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

body.assignment: The architecture work assigns S19 the eval instrument as a product surface: ten eval tables, a frozen `eval_version` under one digest, cases with a write-only `expected`, metrics with a declared grader kind, two literal sign-off pauses, a per-case driver that invokes through the action engine, four graders, a recomputable report and a construction audit. The work replaces the skill's file layout — `results.jsonl`, `traces/` and `report.html` under `.claude/hillclimb/<flow>/` — with rows: the rows are the record, the files are the export. The statement is retrospective, describing the assignment the plan set and the state the 2026-11-28 snapshot carries.
body.scope: In scope are the ten tables, the `approval.eval_id` column and its partial unique index, the thirty-three actions, the `evals:read`, `evals:write` and `evals:approve` scopes, the seven events, the four jobs (`eval.case.run`, `eval.run.tick`, `eval.reap`, `eval.prune`), the three built-in versioned prompts, and screens 15–20 declared so S12 cannot invent them. Out of scope are any UI built here, any model call of S19's own — the runner invokes a registered action and never reconstructs a request — model or embedding hosting, the hillclimb loop and cost search (S20), the benchmark instrument (S17/S18), absorbing `inference-router` or `billing_service`, and grading paths rather than outcomes for agentic subjects.
body.responsibilities: The programme architect authors this retrospective set under the standing delegation; the Architecture Board reviews the Phase A–D artefacts and the SoAW; the SRO is accountable for the capability and the tranche outcome; the eval author, a tenant member holding `evals:write`, builds and edits the instrument; an owner or admin holding `evals:approve` signs the inputs, the grading, the cost and the harness, and starts a full run; S12 owns the six screens the plan declares. The author of the pack is not the accepting role, so the separation of duties holds.
body.acceptance_criteria: The gate is the plan's §7 twelve-step sequence: ten tables row-level-security forced and migration 0026 present in `_sqlx_migrations`; a second pending sign-off refused by `uq_appr_eval_pending`; no run without both sign-offs, with the refusal naming the missing gate and an edit voiding a decided sign-off whose artifact digest no longer matches; the subject input type carrying no `expected` bytes; the held-out wall enforced by access rather than by a prompt; a failed attempt unable to occupy its `(case, rep)` slot; cost derived with a negative column count asserting no eval table has a cost column; the oracle ≈100% and null ≈0% controls plus the judge's three known negatives; the variant grammar, the grade-object shape and the label length enforced as database invariants; no answer-key or sign-off action machine-reachable; the served surface matching `served-spec.lock.json`; and the whole suite under fmt and clippy. `acceptance/programme/S19.toml` is the manifest that carries this gate.
body.contract: The contract commits to one invocation path — the runner calls a registered action through S04's engine and never builds a model request of its own — and to one model call, S10's `completions.create` against `inference-router`. Sign-offs are S06 `approval` rows with a nullable `eval_id` and their own partial unique index, an additive ALTER on S03's table recorded as a contract change, so a sign-off is answerable in the web, Telegram and MCP channels with no second escalation primitive. Cost is derived from `inference_call`, never stored (D23): `inference_call.caller_kind` gains `eval` and the table gains a nullable `eval_run_id` that references S19's run and never a `benchmark_run` id. The answer key is structurally unreachable — no view, export or agent tool carries `expected`, and `evals:approve` is absent from `AGENT_TOOLS` along with `eval_signoffs.*` and `eval_runs.start`.
body.retrospective: This statement is authored on 2026-11-28 for the tranche-8 rework. No contemporaneous statement of architecture work exists: the delivery was recorded in the slice plan and its issues, and the project row stays active. The statement therefore records the terms the plan set, the decisions §9 closes and the open questions §10 leaves, and it names what the snapshot does and does not prove rather than implying a ceremonial review that never happened.

Five drivers, each with a goal and an objective that names its measure. Type diagram; phase A; plateau psa; version 1; status draft; owner the programme architect (conveyor-e2e); reviewer the Architecture Board; review date 2026-11-28; project S19; tranche 8; retrospective under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14. documents.body:
# User Stories — S19 Eval Builder (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

## Personas

The eval author is a tenant member holding `evals:write`: they define the flow, write and import cases, choose metrics and graders, and re-freeze a version when the instrument changes. The sign-off approver is a tenant owner or admin holding `evals:approve`: they decide the input, grading, cost and harness gates and start a full run. The eval consumer is an agent principal on `/mcp`, which reads the instrument, cases and results but never a test-split result, a sign-off or an answer key. The auditor is a quality role that starts a construction audit and decides its findings.

## Stories

As an eval author, I want an eval with a frozen version, cases, metrics and a seeded split, so that a change to the instrument is a new version rather than a silent edit. As a sign-off approver, I want the inputs and the grading to be literal pauses, so that I sign a digest rather than a claim. As an eval author, I want a pilot and then a baseline against the same version, so that my first look at the numbers cannot become the baseline by accident. As an eval consumer, I want a report I can recompute, so that a score arrives with a confidence interval, a noise floor and the count of excluded results.

## Scenarios

Scenario 1, @verify=s19-signoff-gate: a run is refused until both the input and grading sign-offs are decided, and the refusal names the missing gate. Scenario 2, @verify=s19-stale-signoff: an edit after a decided sign-off voids it, and the next run is refused. Scenario 3, @verify=s19-second-pending: a second pending sign-off on the same gate is refused by the partial unique index. Scenario 4, @verify=s19-answer-key: the subject input carries no expected bytes and no case-list view or export returns them. Scenario 5, @verify=s19-heldout: an agent principal reads the instrument but never a test-split result. Scenario 6, @verify=s19-slot: a failed attempt writes eval_attempt_error and leaves the slot empty.

## Verify

The verifying commands are the plan's §7 suite names: `eval_signoff_gate`, `eval_signoff_idx`, `eval_isolation`, `eval_heldout`, `eval_slot` and `eval_controls`, plus the registry suite's `no_eval_signoff_or_answer_key_action_is_machine_reachable`. The plan records them in its historical `rbuild` form, written before the 2026-11-20 owner direction retired local compilation; today the compile and lint verdict comes from the repository's GitHub-hosted preflight and the PR's CI, and every libtest filter is listed by exact name before it is run because a filter that selects zero tests exits zero.

# Acceptance Criteria — S19 Eval Builder (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

## Scenarios

Scenario 1, @verify=s19-schema: the ten eval tables are row-level-security forced and migration 0026 is present and successful in `_sqlx_migrations`. Scenario 2, @verify=s19-signoff-index: a second pending sign-off on the same eval gate is refused by `uq_appr_eval_pending`, not by a check-then-insert. Scenario 3, @verify=s19-run-refused: no run starts without both sign-offs, the refusal names the missing gate, and an edit voids a decided sign-off whose artifact digest no longer matches. Scenario 4, @verify=s19-answer-key: the subject input type carries no `expected` field and no view or export returns it. Scenario 5, @verify=s19-heldout-wall: the held-out half is enforced by the `evals:approve` scope, and an agent reads the instrument but never the held-out half. Scenario 6, @verify=s19-attempt-slot: a failed attempt cannot occupy its `(case, rep)` slot and its error row survives a later success. Scenario 7, @verify=s19-cost-derived: no eval table has a cost column, asserted as a negative column count. Scenario 8, @verify=s19-controls: the oracle scores near 100 percent, the null near 0 percent, an induced error is a classified attempt and the judge fails its three known negatives. Scenario 9, @verify=s19-invariants: the variant grammar, the grade-object shape and the label length are database invariants. Scenario 10, @verify=s19-machine-reach: no answer-key or sign-off action is machine-reachable. Scenario 11, @verify=s19-served-lock: the served surface matches `served-spec.lock.json`. # Definition of Ready — S19 Eval Builder (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

## Independent

S19 ports no old surface: its `parity_ids` is `PENDING-S0` because there is no legacy id to port, and its tables, modules and actions are net-new rather than a rewrite of another member's work. The only couplings are additive contract changes to S03's `approval` and S16's `inference_call`, each recorded in the plan's §9 decisions, so the member can be built and reviewed on its own lane without editing another member's behaviour.

## Negotiable

The scope boundary is explicit and was negotiable in the plan's own terms: no UI is built here — screens 15–20 are declared so S12 cannot invent them — no model call of S19's own, no hosting, no embeddings; the hillclimb loop and the cost search belong to S20; the benchmark instrument stays S17/S18's; and `inference-router` and `billing_service` are not absorbed. What remains negotiable inside the boundary is the implementation shape, not the surface.

## Valuable

The value is one sentence with a number behind it: did this prompt, model or procedure change help? The instrument answers with a confidence interval, a per-case transcript behind every score, and a health audit that says whether the number can be believed. That replaces a directory of `results.jsonl`, `traces/` and `report.html` with rows a person and an agent can both read under the same scopes.

## Estimable

The plan estimates the work as seventeen ordered steps across three parts, each naming its modules and its test target: migration and domain, store, actions, the case driver, the four runner properties, the jobs, the graders, the served-model assertion, the report, the audit, the interop round trip, the scope sites, and the lock regeneration. The module list is explicit — `crates/domain/src/eval`, `crates/store/src/eval`, `crates/actions/src/eval` — so the work can be sized against named files rather than a theme.

## Small

Each part is independently demonstrable: Part A proves an eval reaches `inputs_approved` and a run is refused until it does; Part B proves a five-case pilot yields five complete result rows with a transcript and a grade object; Part C proves a report recomputes from raw rows and an audit reproduces. The copy-on-write version is cheap at the plan's own ceiling of about one hundred cases, and the four jobs reuse S06's queue rather than adding a second one.

## Testable

Every acceptance item is a named test binary with an exact filter, and several are deliberately negative: a column count that must be zero, an index that must refuse a duplicate, a slot that must stay empty after a failure, an oracle that must score near 100 percent and a null that must score near 0 percent. The plan also warns that a libtest filter matching zero tests exits zero, so each filter is listed before it runs; that warning is itself part of testability.

## Dependencies

The project's recorded dependencies are S02, S03, S04, S06, S09, S10, S11 and S16. S04 supplies the registry and invocation engine, S06 the approval and job primitives, S10 the one model call, S11 the procedure and run-step trace sources, S09 the document and object store for export, S02 and S03 the platform schema and control plane, and S16 the inference ledger. S16 is planned and not built at the snapshot — migration 0024 is reserved and unapplied — which is the plan's open question 1 and the reason the cost derivation is the first risk row.

# Definition of Done — S19 Eval Builder (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

## Acceptance criteria

The twelve scenarios of the acceptance-criteria document are the done condition: the ten tables under forced RLS with 0026 in the ledger; the second pending sign-off refused by the partial unique index; no run without both sign-offs and an edit voiding a stale one; the answer key absent from the subject input; the held-out wall enforced by access; a failed attempt unable to occupy its slot; cost derived with a negative column count; the oracle and null controls plus the judge's three negatives; the variant, grade and label invariants; no machine-reachable sign-off or answer-key action; the served surface matching the lock; and fmt, clippy and the suite green.

## Evidence at completion

Each criterion carries an artefact, not a promise: the ledger query for 0026, the index's own refusal test, the sign-off gate suite, `subject_input_carries_no_expected_bytes`, `an_agent_reads_the_instrument_but_never_the_held_out_half`, the slot suite, the negative cost-column count, the controls suite, the constraints suite, the registry test `no_eval_signoff_or_answer_key_action_is_machine_reachable`, the `--print-openapi --check-lock` result and the gate log. The evidence is attached to the delivery PR and re-read at the manifest's receipt; a step GitHub does not carry is the release manager's, and it is never invented.

## Repo gate

The repository's local gate is deliberately sub-second: the hooks run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo metadata --locked` and actionlint on changed workflows. A compiling `cargo` command is denied on local hardware by the owner direction of 2026-11-20, so the compile and lint verdict comes from the GitHub-hosted `preflight.yml`, and the PR's CI is the final gate. One bounded check, never a watch loop; the plan's `rbuild` lines are the historical record of how the slice was gated before that direction.

## Merge and closure

One issue, one branch and exactly one PR per unit, opened non-draft only when the local gate is green and the PR body carries `Closes #<n>`; slices are commits on that branch and never a second PR. The merge queue is the last CI run, and a merge is not shipped until the deployed state is probed. S19's own closure is not this pack's decision: the project stays active and its closure would need the product gate green, the manifest receipt and an approver other than the author, which is why this pack carries no closure keys.

risk.title: S16's inference ledger is planned and not built, so cost derivation has no source at the snapshot
risk.body: S19 derives cost from `inference_call` and stores none (D23), but S16's `inference_call` is planned and not built: migration 0024 is reserved and unapplied. Open question 1's default is to block on S16, and if it slips, to record `usage` on `eval_case_result` from the action response and derive cost with the same arithmetic — identical columns, different source. Until one of the two exists, a report's cost figure has nothing to read, and the risk is recorded rather than hidden behind a placeholder.
risk.response: Hold the cost assertion to the plan's default: block on S16, or record usage on the result row and derive with the same arithmetic, and prove the chosen path in the report suite before any receipt claims cost.

risk.title: A silently substituted served model invalidates every comparison and reads as signal
risk.body: The plan's trap 7 records that `model` must come from the response rather than the config: a silently substituted served model invalidates the comparison, and the failure would look like a regression in the subject. The defence is an assertion that fails the attempt loudly, plus the `judge_is_subject` refusal when the judge model is the subject model. Without both, a routing change upstream becomes a false finding about a prompt.
risk.response: Assert the served model on every attempt and refuse a judge that resolves to the subject; treat any mismatch as a classified attempt error rather than a score.

risk.title: Without the tick finaliser a run stays running forever after its last case
risk.body: N times R jobs finalise nothing on their own. The plan's trap 9 records that without `eval.run.tick` a run stays `running` after its last case, and that the reaper must key on `last_polled_at` rather than on case silence — the S17 lesson. A run that never finalises holds its cost ceiling, blocks the report and makes a cancellation look like a hang, so the finaliser and the heartbeat are load-bearing rather than housekeeping.
risk.response: Prove the finaliser and the heartbeat in the jobs suite, and make the reaper read `last_polled_at`; a run that is silent but heartbeating must not be reaped.

risk.title: Case text is untrusted input and reaches a rendered frame
risk.body: Cases are imported from transcripts and tickets, so their text is untrusted. The plan's trap 10 requires no `inner_html`, html or svg attachments inside a sandboxed frame, binaries as S09 document references, and a size cap on turns. A report or an interop import that renders case text directly would turn an imported transcript into script in a reviewer's session, and a cap that is absent turns one case into an unbounded row.
risk.response: Keep case text out of any raw HTML sink, render it through the one escaping view, store binaries as S09 documents and enforce the turns cap at import.

The benefit is that a change is accepted or refused on evidence a reviewer can recompute from raw rows, rather than on a directory of files whose meaning lived in the method's prose.

The benefit is a provenance property: the audit's requirement that scores before and after a grader change are not comparable becomes a structural refusal instead of a reviewer's memory, and the frozen copy is cheap at the plan's ceiling of about one hundred cases.

# Project Brief — S19 Eval Builder (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

## Outcome

A person defines one flow, builds an input set, signs off the inputs, chooses metrics and a grader, signs off the grading, runs a pilot and then a baseline, and reads a report — all against rows, rather than against a `.claude/hillclimb/<flow>/` directory of `results.jsonl`, `traces/` and `report.html`. The outcome is that "did this prompt, model or procedure change help?" has a number with a confidence interval, a per-case transcript behind every score, and a health audit that says whether the number can be believed at all.

## Boundary

S19 owns the eval instrument: cases, metrics, graders, sign-offs, runs, results, traces, reports, audits and interop. It does not own any UI — screens 15–20 are declared for S12 — a model call of its own, model or embedding hosting, the hillclimb loop and cost search (S20), the benchmark instrument (S17/S18), `inference-router` or `billing_service`, or grading paths rather than outcomes for agentic subjects. It also does not own the approval or job primitives it extends: those stay S06's, with one additive nullable column.

## Reuse sources

The plan's source table names S04's `invoke` and `record_bookkeeping` as the one invocation path, S06's `approval` with `uq_appr_pending` and `job` with its dedupe, lease and attempt columns, S10's `completions.create`, S11's `procedure` and `run_step` as trace sources, and S09's `document` and object store as the export sink. From the skill it carries the method and field set verbatim, the audit's checks as construction requirements, and the report schema's column and turn shapes, including the label length rule; it carries none of the file layout as a requirement.

## Inception units

Part A, steps 1–7: the migration and its ledger proof, the domain state machine, the store, the eval and version actions, the case actions with write-only `expected`, the seeded split, and the sign-off actions. Part B, steps 8–12: the case driver, the four runner properties, the jobs and finaliser, the four graders, the served-model assertion and human labelling. Part C, steps 13–17: the report, the audit, the interop round trip, the scope and lock sites, and the gate. Each step names its module and its test target.

## Dependencies

The project's recorded dependencies are S02, S03, S04, S06, S09, S10, S11 and S16. S16's `inference_call` is planned and not built — migration 0024 is reserved and unapplied — so the plan's open question 1 defaults to blocking on S16, with a fallback that records `usage` on the result row and derives cost with the same arithmetic. S19 in turn unblocks S20's hillclimb and the six S12 screens, and S12 cannot build them before the surface exists.

## Acceptance

`acceptance/programme/S19.toml` carries the acceptance, and the plan's §7 twelve-step gate is its content: the ledger, the sign-off index, the run refusal, the answer-key isolation, the held-out wall, the slot, the negative cost column, the controls, the database invariants, the machine-reach refusal, the served lock and the full suite. The manifest's fifteen checks add the lifecycle set this pack supplies. A green product gate is the build lane's to report, not this pack's to claim.

## Capabilities

Five. Author an eval: a flow becomes a draft, a frozen version, cases, metrics and a seeded split. Sign the instrument: a member's build becomes an approved input and grading set. Run and grade: a pilot or baseline becomes scored cases with transcripts. Report and export: raw rows become a confidence interval or a portable bundle. Audit the instrument: a construction review becomes decidable findings. None of the five owns a model call or a second queue.

## Plan

The plan is `docs/plans/slices/S19-eval-builder.md`, seventeen ordered steps across three parts. The project stays active: this brief accompanies the record set and the two declared outputs, and it does not close the project. The product gate, the S16 ledger dependency and the six screens stay open, and the tranche review reads them from the manifest's receipt rather than from this brief.
